title: Onboard signal pocket summary - ops notes (2026-06-04)
content:
Purpose:
A compact handoff for the week covering model onboarding eval signals, promptset failure archetypes, immediate triage actions, and low-effort experiments to reduce unit failure rate. This is a working notes doc intended for engineers and PMs doing next-touch on new model entries and their promptsets.

Executive snapshot:
- Time window: 2026-05-28 -> 2026-06-03 (7d)
- Primary signal: small-model onboarding cohort (m-small-v3) shows a 9% relative increase in high-confidence hallucinations on knowledge-check prompts vs baseline.
- Secondary signal: reranker precision dropped 5 points for multi-turn e2e flows (not observed in single-turn evals).
- Net impact: two customers on onboarding trials reported notable quality regressions; one trial paused auto-accept.

Top signals (quick numbers):
- Knowledge hallucination rate (KS prompts): baseline 3.2% -> current 3.5% absolute (9% relative), severity: medium
- Reranker precision@1: baseline 82% -> current 77%, severity: medium-high for multi-turn flows
- Truncation-drop: 0.8% of generation tokens clipped unexpectedly on sequences >700 tokens, correlated with new batch packing policy applied on 2026-05-29
- Safety false positives: spike from 0.4% -> 1.1% on policy-check prompts after tokenization change (investigate tokenizer id mapping)

Failure archetypes and examples (representative):
1) Coherent but incorrect facts (hallucination):
   - Prompt: "Who was the CTO of AlphaWave in 2019?"
   - Model response (example): "The CTO was Sarah Milton." (incorrect; no evidence in KB)
   - Signal: high-confidence assertion with low retrieval overlap.

2) Reranker collapse on multi-turn context:
   - Promptset: prior user message + clarifying follow-up -> ground truth candidate at rank 1
   - Observed failure: correct candidate shifted to rank 4; top candidates overly favor short heuristics.
   - Likely cause: interaction between prefix caching and dense-sim similarity delta.

3) Long-context truncation near token boundary:
   - Trigger: inputs with repeated long code blocks or logs
   - Outcome: final completion truncated mid-sentence leading to low usefulness scores.

4) Safety false-positive regressions:
   - Minor paraphrases of benign content flagged; seems tied to tokenizer mapping change + new safety classifier thresholding.

Investigations in progress:
- Tokenizer delta audit (owner: Luca) -> compare token id maps pre/post 2026-05-29; reproduce FP examples with isolated classifier run. Linked JIRA: ML-3129.
- Batching policy rollback test (owner: Ethan) -> A/B: disable new batch-packing for long sequences, measure truncation-drop and p95 latency impact.
- Reranker scoring trace (owner: Maya) -> capture feature deltas across cache hits vs misses; add instrumentation to show similarity drift per-turn.

Immediate action items (owners + ETA):
- Short-term: revert batch packing for sequences >600 tokens in staging (Ethan) - ETA: 2026-06-05
- Medium-term: add 200 adversarial knowledge prompts to onboarding set focused on obscure entity verification (Priya + Applied ML) - ETA: 2026-06-18
- Safety tuning: run classifier ablation with old/new tokenizer mapping and adjust threshold; add 100 false-positive examples to safety eval (Luca) - ETA: 2026-06-10
- Reranker fix: instrument per-turn scoring and add a heuristic fallback to length-normalize candidate scores when delta > 0.18 (Maya) - ETA: 2026-06-11

Low-cost experiments to try this sprint (fast feedback loops):
- System prompt guardband: prepend a short verifier instruction for knowledge-check prompts (e.g., "If unsure, say 'I don't know' and offer steps to verify.") — expected to reduce confident hallucinations; quick A/B across 5% traffic slice.
- Soft-decay on cache confidence: apply decay to cached KV attention weights for tokens older than 3 turns; target reranker edge cases.
- Sampling temp sweep for problematic promptset (0.0 -> 0.4) to evaluate overconfidence vs correctness trade-off.

Data and promptset hygiene notes:
- Coverage gap: < 5% of onboarding promptsets exercise multi-document cross-reference; escalate to data-ops to collect more multi-doc cases.
- Label noise: discovered 12 label flips in recent manual review batch — need a small relabel pass of 340 examples flagged by disagreement>0.4.
- Prompt brittleness: several templates rely on punctuation anchors ("Q:") — add normalized variants to reduce sensitivity.

Customer impact and communication guidance:
- Customer A (trial): paused auto-accept flows — reach out with concrete mitigations (batching rollback + safety tuning) and an ETA for a follow-up demo. Owner: CS lead (Ana Ruiz).
- Customer B: degraded reranking on search-like flows; offer to route to larger instance (m-medium) as interim while fixes land. Owner: Solutions Eng (Rahul).

Next sync and meeting artifacts:
- Weekly onboarding triage: Thu 10:30 PT (agenda: triage owner updates, experiment outcomes, release blockers)
- Add this doc to meeting notes and paste short TL;DR in #am-onboarding Slack before sync.

Open questions / risks:
- Does the tokenizer id change affect other models in the hosted fleet? Need a smoke sweep across 5 representative models.
- If batch packing rollback increases costs >7% for p95 latency-sensitive SLAs, we need a cost-benefit review with product.
- Are the hallucinations concentrated by prompt author or by content domain (finance/legal)? Running domain stratification now.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep experiment windows short (48-72h) for quick signal.
- Flag any customer-visible changes with a pre-rollout notice in Console (route-level).
- Capture before/after qualitative examples for customer-facing case studies.

Relevant tickets/links:
- ML-3129 (tokenizer-safety-audit), ML-3131 (batch-packing-triage), ML-3134 (reranker-instrumentation)
summary: Working operational note: onboarding eval signals, top failure archetypes, triage actions and low-cost experiments for applied-ml team (week of 2026-06-02).
